'''Sviatoslav Yuriyovych''' "'''Svi'''" '''Mykhailiuk''' ({{langx|uk|Святосла́в Ю́рійович Михайлю́к}}, {{IPA|uk|sʲwʲɐtoˈslɑu̯ mɪxɐjˈlʲuk|pron}}; born June 10, 1997) is a Ukrainian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and prior to that, he played for [[Cherkaski Mavpy]] in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]] from 2012 to 2014 and for the [[Ukraine national basketball team|Ukraine national team]] at the [[2014 FIBA World Cup]]. As a reserve with the [[2023–24 Boston Celtics season|2023-24 Boston Celtics]], Mykhailiuk won an NBA championship.

==Early life==
Born in [[Cherkasy]], Ukraine, Mykhailiuk's mother, Inna, is a high school biology teacher, and his father, Iurri, is a college history professor.<ref name="KCStarDodd05222014">Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/2014/05/21/5037687/ukrainian-teenager-sviatoslav.html Ukrainian teenager Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk signs to play for KU basketball team] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140525035502/http://www.kansascity.com/2014/05/21/5037687/ukrainian-teenager-sviatoslav.html |date=May 25, 2014 }}, ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', May 22, 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2014/may/21/sources-ukrainian-wing-mykhailiuk-chooses-ku/?mens_basketball Ukrainian wing Mykhailiuk chooses KU], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', May 21, 2014</ref> He attended high school at Cherkasy First City Gymnasia.<ref name="KUAtleticDept"/>

==College career==
Mykhailiuk received offers from [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref name="KCStarDodd05222014"/><ref name=SaatRCW02182015>{{cite news |last=Saat |first=James |date=February 18, 2015 |title=The American Dream |url=http://contentviewer.adobe.com/s/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly/d9963474-d31e-562e-b24a-2108e9feee08/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly%20Vol%201%20Issue%2024/Cover.html |newspaper=Rock Chalk Weekly |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |publisher=[[Kansas Jayhawks|Kansas Athletics, Inc.]] |volume=1 |issue=24 |access-date=February 18, 2015 |archive-date=February 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150218183954/http://contentviewer.adobe.com/s/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly/d9963474-d31e-562e-b24a-2108e9feee08/Rock%20Chalk%20Weekly%20Vol%201%20Issue%2024/Cover.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On May 21, 2014, Mykhailiuk [[National Letter of Intent|committed]] to play basketball at the [[University of Kansas]] and played for the team during their [[2014–15 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kansas adds Ukrainian star Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24569048/kansas-adds-ukrainian-star-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk|work=CBS.com}}</ref> During his freshman season, he started five of the first seven games of the season, averaging 21.3 minutes a game, but his playing time since then was significantly curtailed.<ref name=SaatRCW02182015/> He scored 11 points while playing 32 minutes in the Orlando Classic Championship game against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] on November 30, 2014.<ref name=SaatRCW02182015/> He was the youngest player in [[Big 12 Conference]] history at 17 years old.<ref name="KUAtleticDept"/>

Returning to Kansas in his sophomore year, Mykhailiuk averaged 5.4 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.9 assists per game in 35 games of the [[2015–16 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2015–16 season]] while hitting 40.2 percent of his three-point shots.<ref name="KUAtleticDept">{{cite news |title=10 Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6589&path=mbball |newspaper=KU Athletics Department |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=April 14, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414004720/http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6589&path=mbball |archive-date=April 14, 2016 }}</ref><ref name="GBedoreLJW04122016">{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=April 12, 2016 |title=Mykhailiuk reveals on Twitter he's coming back for junior season |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/apr/12/mykhailiuk-reveals-twitter-hes-coming-back/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=April 14, 2016 }}</ref> On November 23, 2015, Mykhailiuk scored 18 points against [[Chaminade Silverswords|Chaminade]].<ref name="KUAtleticDept"/> In the first round of the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2016 NCAA basketball tourney]], on March 17, 2016, Mykhailiuk scored 23 points, setting his personal college career scoring record, with 9 of 11 field goals and 4 of 5 threes against the [[2015–16 Austin Peay Governors basketball team|Austin Peay]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Keegan |first=Tom |date=March 17, 2016 |title=Svi Mykhailiuk puts on show in first-round blowout |url=http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/keegan_ratings/2016/mar/17/svi-mykhailiuk-puts-on-show-in-first-rou/ |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=March 25, 2016|quote=Caught fire catching-and-shooting from deep in the corner, dribbled into buckets, got up high on a slam and generally showed off the tools that NBA scouts find intriguing on his way to career-high 23 points (9 of 11 field goals, 4 of 5 threes).}}</ref>

Mykhailiuk returned to Kansas for his junior year of college. On December 22, 2016, in a game against [[UNLV]], Mykhailiuk scored 20 points with 6 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 steals, helping KU to a 71–53 win.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Kansas rolls past UNLV in Las Vegas |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article122596084.html |newspaper=The Kansas City Star |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=January 30, 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=December 22, 2016 |title=Kansas 71 UNLV 53 |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/boxscore.aspx?id=11998&path=mbball |newspaper=[[University of Kansas]] |location=Lawrence, Kansas |access-date=January 30, 2017 |archive-date=March 19, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319110730/http://www.kuathletics.com/boxscore.aspx?id=11998&path=mbball |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="KUAtleticsMykhailiuk">{{cite news |title=10 Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7137 |newspaper=[[University of Kansas]] |location=Lawrence, Kansas |access-date=January 30, 2017 }}</ref> In the UNLV game, Mykhailiuk made 4 of 6 three-point attempts.<ref>Keegan, Tom. [http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/keegan_ratings/2016/dec/22/josh-jackson-moves-to-second-in-season-s/ Josh Jackson moves to second in season standings by putting on first-half show in Vegas], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', December 22, 2016.</ref> In the 2016–17 season, Mykhailiuk averaged 10.6 points per game, 3.5 rebounds per game, and 1.6 assists per game, while shooting 41.5 percent from three-point territory.<ref name="KUAtleticsMykhailiuk"/> On April 12, 2017, Mykhailiuk decided to enter the [[2017 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent, allowing him to return for his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mykhailiuk to enter NBA Draft without an agent|url=http://kuathletics.com/news/2017/4/12/mens-basketball-mykhailiuk-to-enter-nba-draft-without-an-agent.aspx?|website=KUAthletics.com}}</ref> Mykhailiuk opted to return to Kansas for the [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2017–18 season]].

On November 17, 2017, Mykhailiuk scored a career high 27 points in a game against San Diego State.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://m.kusports.com/news/2017/nov/17/svi-mykhailiuk-catches-fire-sparks-blowout-win-ove/?templates.html |title=Svi Mykhailiuk catches fire, sparks blowout win over South Dakota State |last=Chasen |first=Scott |work=KUsports.com |date= November 17, 2017 |access-date= November 19, 2017 }}</ref> He set a school record for 3–pointers made in a season during the Jayhawks 2017–18 season with 115.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kansas senior Svi Mykhailiuk sets three-point record |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas/article/kansas-basketball-senior-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk-sets-jayhawks-three-point-record-116674780/ |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cherkaski Mavpy (2012–2014)===
Prior to playing at Kansas, Mykhailiuk played professionally for [[Cherkaski Mavpy]], his hometown club team, in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]] from 2012 to 2014.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}}

===Los Angeles Lakers (2018–2019)===
On June 21, 2018, Mykhailiuk was selected with the 47th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Joey|last=Ramirez|title=Lakers Select Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk With Draft's 47th Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/180621-lakers-draft-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk|website=NBA.com|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=July 18, 2018}}</ref> On July 10, he signed a three-year, $4.6 million rookie scale contract with the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180710-lakers-sign-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2018|access-date=July 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=July 10, 2018 |title=Sources: Svi Mykhailiuk finalizing 3-year, $4.6M deal with Lakers |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/sources-svi-mykhailiuk-finalizing-3-year-4-6m-deal-lakers-173041358.html |access-date=July 18, 2018 |work=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2019–2021)===
On February 6, 2019, Mykhailiuk was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]], along with a future second-round draft pick, in exchange for [[Reggie Bullock]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-sviatoslav-mykhailiuk|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021)===
On March 13, 2021, Mykhailiuk was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], along with a 2027 second-round draft pick, in exchange for [[Hamidou Diallo]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquire Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/mykhailiuk-210313|website=NBA.com|date=March 13, 2021|access-date=March 13, 2021}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2021–2022)===
On August 31, 2021, Mykhailiuk signed a 2-year deal with the [[Toronto Raptors]] for just over $3.6 million.{{citation needed|date=November 2021}} On August 29, 2022, Mykhailiuk was waived by the Raptors.

===New York Knicks (2022–2023)===
On September 18, 2022, Mykhailiuk signed a 1-year deal with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Lewis|title=Knicks sign Ukrainian wing Svi Mykhailiuk|url=https://nypost.com/2022/09/18/knicks-sign-ukrainian-wing-svi-mykhailiuk/|work=New York Post|date=September 18, 2022|access-date=September 20, 2022}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2023)===
On February 8, 2023, the Knicks reached an agreement to trade Mykhailiuk, [[Ryan Arcidiacono]], [[Cam Reddish]], and draft considerations to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Josh Hart]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jack|last=Maloney|title=Josh Hart-Cam Reddish trade grades: Solid move for Knicks; Blazers take sellers' stance|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/josh-hart-cam-reddish-trade-grades-solid-move-for-knicks-blazers-take-sellers-stance/|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023}}</ref> The following day, the deal was reworked into a four-team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]], with the Hornets receiving Mykhailiuk, the 76ers receiving [[Jalen McDaniels]], the Knicks receiving Hart and the Trail Blazers receiving Arcidiacono, Reddish and [[Matisse Thybulle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Two Second-Round Draft Picks & Svi Mykhailiuk In Four-Team Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-two-second-round-draft-picks-svi-mykhailiuk-in-four-team-deal|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> He made his Hornets debut on February 15, recording 12 points and two rebounds in a 120–110 win over the San Antonio Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|first=Steve|last=Reed|title=BALL HAS TRIPLE-DOUBLE, HORNETS HAND SPURS 14TH LOSS IN ROW|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200873|website=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2023–2024)===
On August 31, 2023, Mykhailiuk signed a 1-year deal with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Sign Svi Mykhailiuk|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/083123-press-release-boston-celtics-sign-forward-svi-mykhailiuk|website=NBA.com|date=August 31, 2023|access-date=August 31, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|title=Guard Svi Mykhailiuk headed to Celtics on one-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/38300819/guard-svi-mykhailiuk-agrees-1-year-deal-celtics|website=ESPN.com|date=August 31, 2023|access-date=August 31, 2023}}</ref> On June 6, 2024, he made his debut in the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] against [[Dallas Mavericks]], becoming the second Ukrainian to achieve this feat following [[Slava Medvedenko]].<ref>{{cite web|title=From Ukraine to NBA Finals: Mykhailiuk's debut highlights Celtics' win|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/ukraine-nba-finals-mykhailiuks-debut-073100047.html|work=Yahoo Sports|date=7 June 2024|access-date=7 June 2024}}</ref> He eventually achieved the NBA title with his club, which won their 18th championship overall.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celtics top Mavericks in Game 5, win record 18th NBA championship|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40375053/celtics-stomp-mavericks-game-5-clinch-record-18th-nba-title|website=ESPN.com|date=18 June 2024|access-date=18 June 2024}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2024–present)===
On 13 August 2024, Mykhailiuk signed a 4-year deal with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Svi Mykhailiuk|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-svi-mykhailiuk|website=NBA.com|date=13 August 2024|access-date=1 September 2024}}</ref> On November 6, 2025, Mykhailiuk scored an NBA career high 28 points in a game against [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Garrett|last=Ball|title=Svi Mykhailiuk puts up career-high 28 points in win|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/550401/svi-mykhailiuk-puts-up-career-high-28-points-win.php|website=fantasypros.com|date=6 November 2025|access-date=7 November 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
===Ukrainian junior national team===
In the summer of 2013, Mykhailiuk played with the Ukrainian Under-16 junior national team in the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]]. He was selected to the All-Tournament Team,<ref>fiba.com [http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_kG7Aj2BgG76iJfEHEBQN,2.articleMode_on.html 2013 U16 All-Tournament Team] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820141011/http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/coid_kG7Aj2BgG76iJfEHEBQN,2.articleMode_on.html |date=August 20, 2016 }}</ref> after completing an outstanding championship, averaging 25.2 points, 8.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game.<ref>fiba.com [http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/cid_z8jOMILgHCsbXTL1wG4sq0.teamID_2183.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.playerID_99106.html Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk 2013 U16 stats] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141229021209/http://u16men.fibaeurope.com/en/cid_z8jOMILgHCsbXTL1wG4sq0.teamID_2183.compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2013.roundID_9441.playerID_99106.html |date=December 29, 2014 }}</ref>

Mykhailiuk played for the Ukrainian under-20 junior national team in the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] in [[Helsinki]].<ref name="U20FIBALawJWJuly2016">{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=July 17, 2016 |title=Mykhailiuk unloads for 14 in U-20 tourney |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/jul/17/mykhailiuk-unloads-14-u-20-tourney/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=July 18, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Junior Male Team (U20) |url=http://fbu.ua/national-team/team-621/ |newspaper=[[Ukrainian Basketball Federation]] |location=[[Kyiv]] |access-date=July 18, 2016 |language=uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=July 17, 2016 |title=Game Story |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20/2016/1707/Ukraine-Serbia#tab=game_story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160720171346/http://www.fiba.com/europe/u20/2016/1707/Ukraine-Serbia#tab=game_story |url-status=live |archive-date=July 20, 2016 |newspaper=FIBA |location=[[Mies, Switzerland|Mies]], [[Switzerland]] |access-date=July 18, 2016 }}</ref> During the tournament, Mykhailiuk led his team in scoring, at 14.9 points per game, in seven tourney games.<ref name="GBedoreLawJW07252016">{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=July 25, 2016|title=Mykhailiuk scores 21 in final loss |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2016/jul/25/mykhailiuk-scores-21-final-loss/?mens_basketball |newspaper=[[Lawrence Journal-World]] |location=[[Lawrence, Kansas]] |access-date=July 25, 2016}}</ref> He hit 36.8 percent of his floor shots.<ref name="GBedoreLawJW07252016"/> Mykhailiuk shot 47.2 percent from two-point and 19 percent from three-point territory.<ref name="GBedoreLawJW07252016"/> He made 85.7 percent of his free throws and also grabbed 5.6 rebounds a game, with 2.7 assists, 4.7 turnovers, and 2.1 steals per game.<ref name="GBedoreLawJW07252016"/>

He played for the Ukrainian under-20 team again in the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he was the leading scorer of the tournament, averaging 20.4 points per game.

===Ukrainian senior national team===
Mykhailiuk played with the senior men's [[Ukraine national basketball team]], which competed at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], in [[Spain]], from August 30 to September 14.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=August 25, 2014 |title=Chillin' out: 'Svi' excused from Challenge |url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2014/aug/25/chillin-out-svi-excused-challenge/ |newspaper=Lawrence Journal-World |location=Lawrence, Kansas |publisher=The World Company |access-date=August 25, 2014 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Following [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of Ukraine]] on February 23, 2022, Mykhailiuk along with the only other Ukrainian NBA player, [[Alex Len]], released a statement condemning the invasion. The statement read "A great tragedy befell our dear homeland of Ukraine. We categorically condemn the war. Ukraine is a peaceful, sovereign state inhabited by people who want to control their own destiny. We pray for their families, friends, and relatives and all the people who are in the territory of Ukraine. We hope for an end to this terrible war as soon as possible. Dear fellow Ukrainians, hold on! Our strength is in unity! We are with you!"<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Svi Mykhailiuk|user=sviat_10|number = 1496972690623807492 |date=February 24, 2022|title=Ні Війні! (Ukrainian)}}</ref>
